title: Replit alternatives
summary: Replit alternatives: candidate paths, switching costs and reasons to keep the original.

sections.heading: Match the reason to a candidate
paragraphs: Lovable and Bolt can be evaluated for another app-building workflow. Claude Code is a repository-work alternative for someone prepared to choose and manage hosting separately.

sections.heading: When to keep the original
paragraphs: Keep Replit if operational convenience is valuable and current billing is acceptable after verification. Moving only the code does not move secrets, data or domain configuration.

sections.heading: Migration rehearsal
paragraphs: Create a copy of the project, remove production secrets, export data using a documented method and run the tests in the candidate workflow. Compare the work needed to restore service after a failed change. Keep the original until the rehearsal succeeds.

verdict: Separate replacing the builder from replacing the hosting and development environment.
bestFor: Existing Replit users with a specific workflow, budget or ownership constraint
notFor: Readers expecting a replacement to move code, data and infrastructure automatically
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.

pros.text: Lovable documents code synchronization to GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket for teams evaluating a repository-centered handoff.
Bolt documents importing an existing GitHub repository as well as its JavaScript web-app and Expo paths.

cons.text: Replit checkpoints are described as in-platform recovery snapshots; they do not establish a tested independent export or recovery route.
Lovable credits cover different build and runtime activities, so a credit total alone is not a comparable estimate of the full application lifecycle.

faqs.question: Do Replit checkpoints replace an external backup?
faqs.answer: The documentation describes checkpoints inside Replit. Test a separate code export and recovery process if the project must operate outside the platform.

faqs.question: Which candidates document Git-based project movement?
faqs.answer: Lovable documents sync with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket; Bolt documents GitHub repository import and version control. Test runtime services separately.

faqs.question: What should I verify about Lovable model training before choosing a builder?
faqs.answer: Its 2026-09-15 Privacy Policy says Customer Content and Usage Data may be used for training, with a free settings opt-out that takes effect prospectively on any plan; it excludes Business/Enterprise content and usage data and app end-user data. The August 2026 Terms and November 2025 DPA distinguish data scopes differently, so verify the actual workspace agreement and setting.

faqs.question: Does choosing an EU Lovable Cloud region keep all project data in the EU?
faqs.answer: Lovable says Lovable Cloud offers EU, US and Asia Pacific regions and that selected-region Cloud data does not move across regions by default. Its Privacy Policy also says Lovable and service providers process Personal Data in multiple countries, including the US. This does not establish the actual workspace selection or locations for connected services and model providers.
